entry.title: Contemporaneous Transmission Networks and Systemic Risk in European Banking
entry.summary:
We study how contemporaneous equity-return transmission shapes systemic exposure among 51 listed European banks. Using a recursive non-Gaussian network model on volatility-standardized returns, we construct two market-capitalization-weighted measures based on direct and indirect transmission effects: the Systemic Impact Score (SIS), capturing a bank's potential influence on other institutions, and the Systemic Vulnerability Score (SVS), capturing its exposure to disturbances originating elsewhere. The fitted network reveals distinct transmitting and receiving roles, highlighting differences between institutions with substantial outward influence and those with high incoming sensitivity.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance #infosec

entry.title: Characterizing Maximum Nash Welfare: Envy-Freeness and Proportionality
entry.summary:
When allocating indivisible goods, the maximum Nash welfare rule is known to be the unique welfarist rule satisfying envy-freeness up to one good. We strengthen this characterization by showing that envy-freeness up to one good can be replaced by substantially weaker fairness requirements: envy-freeness up to $k$ goods or proportionality up to $k$ goods, for any fixed $k$. Our characterization holds even for profiles with identical goods.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #market-design #decision-theory

entry.title: Sybil-Proofness of Generalized Adaptive Clinching and Implications for Blockchain Mechanism Design
entry.summary:
The adaptive clinching auction of Dobzinski, Lavi, and Nisan (FOCS'08) is a cornerstone of mechanism design with budget-constrained bidders, and it has since inspired a broad range of extensions to substantially richer market settings. Adaptive clinching enjoys compelling guarantees: it is Pareto optimal, and truthful bidding is a dominant strategy whenever budgets cannot be overreported. In many real-world environments, however, identities are cheap to create, making resilience to Sybil attacks an additional requirement.

entry.title: Fuji: The Shape, Composition, and Spread of Demand Bursts on Robinhood Chain
entry.summary:
Demand on blockchain-based marketplaces arrives in bursts and at a high rate. On these platforms the data are completely visible, which makes it feasible to compare the bursty demand against the usual load. The congestion manifests as an increased demand for gas, the primary resource a blockchain sells.

entry.title: Beliefs Over Contracts -- by Francis Annan, Collin B. Raymond. We study how firms choose among incentive contracts and how accurately managers predict their effects.
entry.summary:
We study how firms choose among incentive contracts and how accurately managers predict their effects. Using a survey of managerial beliefs and a large-scale field experiment, we randomly assign agents at the market level to several widely used, expenditure-equivalent incentive schemes. In the field, the best-performing contract raises weekly firm profit by over 55% relative to the status quo, despite being ranked lower by managers, whereas the worst-performing contract performs as predicted.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #agents

entry.title: Strategic Monetary Policy in Open Economies -- by Louphou Coulibaly, Charles Engel
entry.summary:
We examine optimal non-cooperative monetary policy in a two-country New Keynesian setting with complete financial markets and pricing to market for goods. In contrast to the case in which the law of one price holds for goods, currency misalignments are an important consideration even for self-oriented policymakers. Financial markets are critical in the analysis.

entry.title: The Occupational Ladder: Implications for Life-Cycle Wage Dynamics -- by Henry E. Siu, Kelly Foley, Matias Cortes
entry.summary:
Some occupations pay higher wages than others, even conditional on worker characteristics, implying that occupations can be ranked on a ladder. We develop a simple decomposition to study the role this occupational ladder plays in average wage growth and in the fanning out of wages over the life cycle. We present three main findings.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics
